summary_en: This study compares continuing a Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BTKi) alone with adding venetoclax to the BTKi in veterans with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). Both drugs are taken by mouth as pills; the comparison arm keeps the BTKi alone as long as it is working, while the other arm adds venetoclax to the BTKi for 12 cycles (one year), then stops both pills and monitors participants closely. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
summary_es: Este estudio compara continuar solo con un inhibidor de la tirosina quinasa de Bruton (BTKi) frente a añadir venetoclax al BTKi en veteranos con leucemia linfocítica crónica (LLC) o linfoma linfocítico de pequeñas células (LLPC). Ambos medicamentos se toman por vía oral en forma de pastillas; el grupo de comparación mantiene solo el BTKi mientras le funcione, y el otro grupo añade venetoclax al BTKi durante 12 ciclos (un año), luego suspende ambas pastillas y los participantes son vigilados de cerca. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Diagnosed with CLL or SLL, with the blood cell or lymph node criteria stated in the record
Currently receiving a BTK inhibitor (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, or zanubrutinib) for at least six months
BTK inhibitor dose stable for at least the past three months
Performance status 0 to 2 on the standard ECOG scale
Detectable or measurable disease, with low tumor lysis syndrome risk (lymph nodes under 5 cm, lymphocyte count under 25 x 10^9/L)
not_for: Disease that progressed on BTK inhibitor therapy before starting study treatment
Previous treatment with the combination of a BTK inhibitor and venetoclax
History of Richter's transformation or prolymphocytic leukemia
Heart failure (NYHA class III or IV), unstable angina, or uncontrolled arrhythmia
Taking active anticoagulation with heparin or warfarin, or needing more than 20 mg daily of prednisone or equivalent
